about: The Delvers' mine: a deep site generated from what the mine was for. Levels follow the vein down: the adit level where ore was hauled out, the haulage level round the shaft bottom, the drowned level below the pumps, and the breach where the last gallery broke into something not theirs. Each level is a spine of rooms (a role, or ?role for one that may not be there), with branches off it and loops through it; connectors join the levels (the cage in the shaft, the ladders in the winze, the ore pass, the sealed stair). Roles give each room its names and its scene; {old} is the mine's old name, {makers} the Delvers, {successors} the kingdom after them. Written by hand.

plan.seen: a timbered adit in a hillside

names: a crawl through the old workings
a gallery the props have half let go of

buried: The stair comes down into a timbered mouth cut square into the rock under {town}. It is the height of a man and the width of a cart. Its lintel is a single oak beam, black with age. Cold air comes out of it, steady as breath.
scenes: A timbered mouth opens in the hillside, the height of a man and the width of a cart. Its lintel is a single oak beam, black with age. The spoil of the old workings spreads below it in a grey fan that the heather has never taken. Cold air comes out of it, steady as breath.

The adit runs straight into the hill, just high enough to walk upright. Oak props hold its roof every few paces. Ruts are worn into the floor where the tubs ran, and a rail of black wood still lies in one of them.
A gallery runs on into the hill, dry and cold, the props on either hand furred with white mould. Somewhere ahead water drips into water.

Two galleries cross under a roof cut higher, to turn the tubs. Tools hang on a rack on the wall, rusted into one shape. Chalk marks on the props point each way: a star toward the shaft, an open hand toward the stopes.
A long chamber where the vein was taken out from floor to roof. Walls of stacked stone hold up the hanging wall. The pale ore is gone; what is left glitters faintly where your light touches it.
The vein was wide here, and the Delvers followed it up and down into a hall of their own making. Its roof is lost in the dark above your light. Rubble lies in heaps where they left it.

The gallery widens into a chamber round the head of a shaft. A winding wheel taller than a man stands over the hole on a frame of oak and bronze. A chain runs from it down into the dark. Whatever hangs on the chain is somewhere below.
A square hole drops through the floor in a corner. Ladders lashed to its side go down, one below another, out of your light. The miners' way down, not the ore's: for those who did not trust the cage.
A chimney of rough rock goes straight up out of the gallery roof; daylight shows at the top of it, very small. Iron rungs are set in one side, and the air pours up it the way water goes down a drain.

A funnel of smooth rock opens in the floor: the ore pass, down which the Delvers tipped what they cut to the level below. Its sides are polished by a hundred years of stone going down, too smooth to climb.
A side chamber with a hearth cut into the rock and a smoke-hole above it. An anvil stands on a block of oak. Here the Delvers mended their picks; the floor is black with a century of scale.
The shaft comes down into a stone-lined chamber. Tubs stand in a line on the rails, some still heaped with pale ore that nobody hauled up.
The main road of the level is a broad gallery with a rail down its middle. Refuges are cut in the walls every fifty paces, to step into when the tubs came.
The haulage runs on, straight as a rule, and the rail in it is iron here, not wood. Your steps come back to you from far ahead.
A long hall cut in the rock, with benches of the same rock. At the end a hearth's smoke-hole goes up into the dark. Names are cut on every wall, hundreds of them, each with a small star beside it.
Racks and bins line both walls: rope rotted to dust, lamp-oil dried to varnish in its jars. The iron tools are stacked neatly, as if for the next shift.

A niche cut deep into the wall, and in it a lump of the pale ore the size of a child's head, polished by hands. Offerings lie in front of it: a pick-head, a ring, a child's shoe, all furred with rust.
A wheel as tall as two men stands in a pit, under a race cut to bring water onto its paddles. Buckets on a chain hang from its axle into a well-shaft. The shaft goes down to the level below.
The ladders end in a small chamber at the haulage level. A bench is cut in the wall, where the climbers sat to get their breath.
The ore pass ends above a stone bin as big as a room, half full of rubble and ore tipped down from above. A door at the bottom of the bin let the ore out into the tubs.
At the end of the level the haulage way stops. A stair cut in the rock goes down from it, steep, worn hollow by the Delvers' boots. The air that comes up it is wet.
The stair comes down onto a floor of grey silt, ridged where the water went out of it. The walls are black to the roof with the water's mark.
A long gallery that was under water for longer than anyone remembers. Silt lies a foot deep, and in it lie a lamp, a boot and the bones of a rat.
A hall where the star-iron was smelted. A furnace like a beehive, taller than a house, stands with its mouth black and its bellows rotted to rags. The floor is glass in places where the slag ran.
Past the furnace a rough cut goes down at a steep slant, hacked out fast by many hands. The pick-marks are still sharp. The air coming up it is colder than the rest of the mine.

A small square room with a door of bronze a hand thick, standing open on its pivot. Shelves along the walls held the reckoning of the mine: tallies, weights, a great balance whose pans are green with age.
The vein shows in the face of the gallery as a seam of pale ore as thick as your arm. In your light it shimmers slowly under the surface, rising and falling like breath.

The rough cut ends at a hole in the rock that is not the Delvers' work. Its sides are smooth as the inside of a bell, and faintly warm. It opens into a space too large for your light to find the far side.

A cavern no one cut: a dome of rock streaked with the pale ore. Here the ore gives a light of its own, grey as a winter morning, enough to see by. The Delvers' ladders and props end at its edge as if their makers had stopped there, all at once.
A low-roofed pocket of the cavern. The Delvers' things lie on its floor in a neat row: picks, a lamp, a cloak.

At the back of the cavern the floor opens in a crack you could walk into sideways. It goes down, smooth-sided and faintly warm, further than anything the Delvers dug. A smell comes up it like the inside of a shell.
The Delvers' last gallery, cut in haste. The timbering stops halfway along, and past it the walls are black and glassy where the rock was fired.
At the bottom of the cavern the vein comes together in a mass of star-iron as big as a cart, rooted in the rock and lit from within. It hums, very low, a note you feel in your teeth more than hear.

A spring comes out of the rock here and runs off along a channel cut in the floor. Beside it a race goes off into the dark, cut to carry the water to the levels below. A bronze gate stands where the two divide.

incomers.label: the gnolls
incomers.role: a pack of gnolls come in from outside, denning where the old dwellers were

groups.label: the rats
groups.role: rats gone bold in the dark

groups.label: the cave spiders
groups.role: spiders as big as a cat, nesting in the props

groups.label: the bats
groups.role: bats in the roof

groups.label: the goblins
groups.role: goblins who have made a home of the upper galleries

groups.label: the wolves
groups.role: a pair of wolves that have made the old workings their den

groups.label: the ghouls
groups.role: things that were miners once, and still go down to work

groups.label: the bone hounds
groups.role: the Delvers' dogs, still on their watch

groups.label: the cave hounds
groups.role: pale hounds with no eyes to speak of

groups.label: the mud
groups.role: mud that moves where the pump-shaft overflows

groups.label: the forge-imps
groups.role: small things of smoke and cinder, come up with the forge's last fire

groups.label: the haulers
groups.role: iron haulers of the Delvers that still drag their sledges along the haulage

groups.label: the shining one
groups.role: a thing of star-iron and light that walks the drowned galleries

groups.label: the xill
groups.role: red things that step out of the rock, and lay their eggs in what they catch

groups.label: the render
groups.role: a grey bulk that tears open the stone for what lives in it

groups.label: the vein-born
groups.role: things the ore has made of itself

groups.label: the ooze
groups.role: something grey that lives in the silt

groups.label: the thing from the rift
groups.role: a horned shape that came up through the breach the Delvers made

keeper.label: the thing in the vein
keeper.role: what the Delvers broke into, which thinks

words.Warns: A pressure comes into your head, not quite a voice. It is aware of you, and it is not afraid.
words.Flinches: The light of a summer noon comes into the cavern with you, and the pressure in your head becomes a sound like a held breath let go. The thing in the vein draws back from the light, slowly, the way a tide goes out, into the rift at the back of the cavern.

bane.seen: On the top shelf, behind the balance, stands a jar of thick old glass stoppered with lead, and it is full of light: not lamplight, but daylight, the colour of noon.
bane.cut: IT CANNOT BEAR THE NOON. THE PAYMASTER KEEPS NOON IN A JAR.
bane.fact: What the Delvers walled in below their mine cannot bear the light of noon; their paymaster kept noon in a jar.
bane.aim: Find the noon the paymaster kept in a jar, before you go down to what the Delvers walled in.

objective.text: The Delvers went down after the star-iron until their last gallery broke into the heart of the vein, and what lived in it. Whoever brings up the heart has what the Delvers died for.
objective.goal: Bring the heart of the vein up out of {name}, from below the Delvers' last gallery.
objective.raised: In the daylight the heart of the vein, up out of {name} at last, is heavier than it was in the dark, and it has stopped humming.

rumours: 'The Delvers' mine at {name}? There is still ore down there, they say, the pale kind. Nobody goes below the first level. The cage hangs in the shaft and the wheel will not turn.'
'My grandfather went into {name} after the star-iron. He said the stair at the bottom was walled up by the Delvers themselves, and there was writing on it, and he came back up without reading it.'

land.blight: The heather stops a long stride short of the adit mouth all round, scorched back, and grows again beyond. Nothing nests in the spoil.

signs.woodcraft: There is no track into the adit that is not a man's, and the foxes' runs bend wide of it. Only at noon, with the sun full on the hillside, do the ravens come down and sit on the spoil.
signs.digging: The last of the spoil, at the top of the heap, is not the same stone as the rest. It is black and glassy, as if fired. The Delvers' last gallery broke into something that was not rock.

land.healed: The heather has begun to creep back toward the adit mouth, and a wheatear has a nest in the spoil.

camp.later: The same party camped here too, further in: the ring of stones again, smaller, and less left beside it than above, a blanket and an empty water-skin, as if they were travelling lighter by now.
camp.scene: A party camped here not long ago, on the dry floor between the props: a ring of stones round dead ashes, a bedroll stiff with damp. A pack lies with its straps cut, and nobody came back for it.
journal: A damp notebook, the last pages written small to save them. 'The cage is at the bottom and the wheel will not turn: rusted. Ebbe says a bar under the axle would free it, if we had brought one. The ladders in the winze are sound as far as we went. Something lives in the props by the adit; it bit Edda.'

A damp notebook, the last pages written small. 'The stair at the end of the haulage is walled up, and there is writing on it nobody can read. Under the pump-room the shaft is full of water. Edda says the wheel was turned by water from above, and that is what the dry channel up by the spring is for. She wants to try it. I want to go home.'
A damp notebook, the last page hardly legible. 'Past the furnace the cut goes down, and the cold comes up it like breath. Brann went down with a rope. The rope came up.'
A notebook with one line in it, written by someone lying down: 'it is not asleep'.

outside: Spoil heaps run down the hillside in grey fans the heather has never taken. Above them a timbered mouth opens into the hill. Cut into the beam in the old script, worn but whole: {oldup}.
under: The stair ends at a timbered mouth cut square into the rock, older than the town's cellars above it. Cut into the beam in the old script, worn but whole: {oldup}.

trade.topic: what the old workings are worth
trade.says: turns a lump of something pale over in the light. 'Bring me star-iron and I will pay for it. Fifteen coin a lump, and no questions.'

brought.ask: Ask {merchant} where the rest of the star-iron went
brought.says: {merchant} weighs the lump in one hand, then the other. 'This is off the top of the vein. The Delvers had the best of it out before my grandmother was born.' The lump goes on the scale. 'They followed the rest down the shaft. The cage hangs there still. Their last gallery broke into the heart of the vein, the old men say, and into what lived in it. Nobody has been below the shaft since.'

trade.shown: A lump of star-iron sits at the end of {merchant}'s counter, holding down a pile of bills where buyers can see it.

hook.below: 'Down the cage?' says {keeper}, and stops wiping the counter. 'Below the first level. My grandfather's grandfather went down it and never came up.' A long look at your boots. 'You'll have something on the house, then. Nobody here believes you, mind.'
hook.home: 'The heart of the vein?' {keeper} turns it over in both hands, and it is heavier than it looks, and warm. 'My grandfather's grandfather went down for that and never came up. There is no paying for it. You eat here tonight, and sleep, and nobody takes your coin.'

ore.name: a lump of star-iron
ore.text: Pale ore, heavier than it looks, that glitters faintly in the dark.

negligible.name: a Delver's pay-token
negligible.text: A token of silver stamped with a pick and a star: what a Delver was paid a shift in, and what the paymaster took back for bread.

negligible.name: a string of star-iron beads
negligible.text: Beads of the pale ore on a cord gone hard as wire, worn by someone who dug it.

negligible.name: a bronze tally-board
negligible.text: A board of bronze pegs where a shift's tubs were counted, the last count still in it.

minor.name: a Delver's silver lamp
minor.text: A miner's lamp of silver, not tin: a foreman's, or a gift. It would still light, with oil in it.

minor.name: a Delver's ring
minor.text: A heavy ring with a star cut in it, the mark the Delvers put on what was theirs.

minor.name: a small star-iron ingot
minor.text: A bar of the smelted ore no longer than a finger, pale and heavier than it looks.

major.name: a star-iron ingot
major.text: A bar of smelted star-iron the length of a forearm, stamped with the Delvers' star: what the mine was dug for, made.

major.name: the paymaster's seal
major.text: A seal of gold and star-iron that sealed the mine's reckonings. Anyone in the old kingdom's lands would know it.

major.name: a reliquary of the vein
major.text: A little house of silver with a sliver of the ore inside it behind crystal, kept by the Delvers as other folk keep a saint's bone.

grand.name: a crown of star-iron
grand.text: A plain circlet of the pale ore that gives off a light of its own in the dark: made for someone the Delvers followed down.

grand.name: a cup cut from one crystal
grand.text: A cup carved from a single crystal found in the vein, so clear you see the light of your torch through the wine that is not in it.

groups.label: the goblin chief
groups.role: the biggest of the goblins, in a Delver's iron helm too big for him

groups.label: the shift-boss
groups.role: a shadow that still walks the haulage, calling the shifts

groups.label: the pale pack
groups.role: the biggest of the cave hounds, and their leader

groups.label: the overseer
groups.role: the last overseer of the mine, who will not stop counting

groups.label: the furnace breath
groups.role: heat that would not go out of the furnace, and walks

groups.label: the vein's warden
groups.role: rock that has learned to stand up

groups.label: the burning one
groups.role: a shape of fire that walks the bottom of the breach, where the deep heat comes up

warlords.scene: The warlords who came after the Delvers built a gate of squared timbers across the adit and cut slots in the rock beside it for bowmen. It stands open now, its bar rotted through.

document.name: the words burned into the gate-beam
document.shut: Words are burned into the gate's crossbeam with a hot iron, in the kingdom's letters, not the old script.
document.label: Read the words on the gate-beam
document.text: BY THE LORD OF {kingdomup} THIS WORKING IS HELD. NONE BELOW THE CROSSING.

barrier.name: the warlords' barricade
barrier.text: A barricade of ore-tubs and timber, chained together, closes the gallery to the winze: whoever held the adit did not want anything coming up from below.
barrier.down: The warlords' barricade lies dragged apart across the gallery.
barrier.label: Drag the barricade apart

abbots.scene: The brothers who came after the Delvers made a chapel of their hall: a sign is cut over the hearth, and the long table has been turned into an altar.

document.name: the brothers' tablet
document.shut: A slate tablet hangs on a nail by the altar, written over in a careful hand.
document.label: Read the brothers' tablet
document.text: The brothers of {kingdom} kept a lamp here for the Delvers' dead, and blessed the wall on the stair a second time. Let no one take the lamp away, and let no one take the wall down.

valuable.name: a chapel cup of pewter and star-iron
valuable.text: A plain cup the brothers made out of what the Delvers left, for their altar underground.

princes.scene: Merchant-princes reopened the upper workings for a few years after the Delvers: the store-room was their tally-house, and its door is painted with a ship.

document.name: a company ledger
document.shut: A ledger bound in oiled leather lies on the shelf, swollen shut with damp.
document.label: Prise the ledger open and read it
document.text: Ledger of the {kingdom} company at the old workings: forty tubs of ore the first year, eleven the second, three the third. The men will not go below the second level, whatever they are paid. The working given up.

valuable.name: a purse of merchant ducats
valuable.text: Gold coins with a ship on one side: a merchant-prince's wages, never paid out.

plague.scene: When the plague came, the town shut its sick in the old stope. There are bones along the stone walls, and white quicklime over them, and a sign scratched on every prop.

winter.scene: In the long winter whole families lived down here, where it was warmer than above: hearths of stacked stone along the walls, and a child's carving of a cow left on a ledge.

heirs.scene: In the war of the heirs an heir's man came down here with his lord's coin to hide: there are boot-marks in the old ore dust that are not the Delvers'.

hidden.found: Under the dead ore at the bottom of the bin, a strongbox an heir's man buried in the war of the heirs.

valuable.name: an heir's strongbox
valuable.text: An iron box with a broken seal, full of the coin of a kingdom that no longer exists.

raiders.scene: Raiders from over the sea kept their plunder in the adit one summer: their carved post still stands at the mouth, a ship's figurehead with its face hacked off.

shortcuts.unmade: The cage stands at the shaft bottom, unhooked from its chain, its sheaves dry and stiff. Wound from above, it would come down here in one long drop.
shortcuts.made: The cage hangs hooked to its chain, its sheaves oiled.
shortcuts.make: Oil the cage's sheaves and hook it to the chain
shortcuts.geared: The cage cannot be hooked to a chain that will not run: the wheel above is seized.
shortcuts.told: The cage runs now. From the way in, the tub-road and the cage take you straight down to the shaft bottom.

shortcuts.unmade: Beside the foot of the stair a narrow raise goes straight up into the rock. Ladders are pinned to its side. The lowest lengths have rotted away.
shortcuts.made: Your rope hangs down the raise beside the ladders, made fast at the top.
shortcuts.make: Climb the raise and leave a rope hanging in it
shortcuts.told: Your rope hangs in the raise now. From the way in, you can go straight down it to the foot of the sealed stair.

shortcuts.unmade: Over the breach a chimney goes up through the rock, smooth as the hole itself, toward the Delvers' workings. A cold draught falls down it from far above.
shortcuts.made: Your rope hangs down the warm chimney, made fast at the top.
shortcuts.make: Climb the chimney and leave a rope hanging in it
shortcuts.told: Your rope hangs in the chimney now. From the way in, you can go straight down it to the breach.
shortcuts.way: the rope in the warm chimney

winch.seized: The winding wheel is seized: rust has locked its axle, and the chain hangs slack down the shaft. Somewhere below, the cage sits at the bottom.
winch.turning: The winding wheel turns, stiffly, and the chain runs over it; the cage can be wound up and let down.
winch.shut: The cage is at the bottom of the shaft, and the wheel that would bring it up will not turn.

seal.standing: A wall of dressed stone stands across the stair, built in a hurry, its mortar slopped and run.
seal.broken: The wall across the stair lies in pieces on the steps, and the way down is open.
seal.rebuild: Build the wall back up across the stair
seal.words: the words cut in the wall
seal.unread: Words are cut deep into the stones of the wall, in the old script. Someone who reads the old script could say what they mean.
seal.read: {oldup} SHUT THIS. WE WENT TOO FAR DOWN, AND WHAT WE FOUND WE LEFT THERE. {FATE}
seal.readLabel: Read what is cut in the wall
seal.told: Read aloud, the old words say plainly enough what the makers shut in below, and what it cannot bear.

vent.found: Where the draft goes: behind the rubble at the end of the stope, a way into the air shaft.
vent.sign: A draft moves your light, steadily, toward the end of the chamber, where the rubble is heaped highest.
vent.rungs: the iron rungs in the air shaft

drowned.flooded: Black water fills the gallery to its roof.
drowned.deep: The stair goes down into black water, which stands to within a hand of the roof of the gallery ahead. Your light goes into it and does not come back.
drowned.going: The water has gone down: the tops of the gallery's props stand out of it now, black and dripping, and it is still going.
drowned.gate: the bronze gate in the channel
drowned.gateShut: The bronze gate stands across the race, and the spring runs on down its own channel and away.
drowned.gateOpen: The gate is swung across the old channel, and the spring goes roaring away down the race into the dark.
drowned.open: Swing the gate across, and turn the spring down the race
drowned.shut: Swing the gate back, and let the spring run its own way
drowned.slack: The bucket-chain hangs slack from the wheel's axle; the pawl that would hold it to the axle is knocked out of its seat.
drowned.engaged: The bucket-chain is set on the axle, and goes round with the wheel.
drowned.engage: Knock the pawl home, and set the bucket-chain on the axle
drowned.drained: From the pump-shaft comes a new sound: the buckets coming up empty, full of air.
drowned.running: Water pours down the race onto the wheel, which turns with a noise like a mill; the buckets come up full out of the shaft and tip into the drain.
drowned.idle: Water pours down the race and the wheel spins on nothing: the buckets hang still in the shaft.
drowned.dry: The race above the wheel is dry, and the wheel stands still. Down the well-shaft there is the sound of standing water.
drowned.heard: Far below, very faint through the rock, something is turning.

marks.name: the marks on the adit's post-stone
marks.unread: A post-stone stands at the mouth of the workings, cut with marks in the old script.
marks.read: The marks are the makers' own, cut when the first seam was opened: who dug here, and what they believed lay below.
marks.label: Read the marks on the post-stone

cache.cue: In the end wall of the hall one stretch is boarded over with planks, nailed tight. The rest of the hall is bare rock.
cache.searched: Behind the planks in the end wall the rock is cut square: a store, boarded over.
cache.found: Behind the boarded stretch of the hall's end wall, a store-room cut into the rock.
cache.mark: the paymaster's mark on the planks
cache.markseen: A mark is burned into the middle plank: a pick and a star, the Delvers' paymaster's. A word in later letters runs across it.
cache.readlabel: Make out the word burned across the paymaster's mark
cache.lore: The pick and star are the Delvers' own; the word across them is the kingdom's: SEALED. The planks are nailed from this side, and the nails are loose.
cache.loreno: The word is burned too deep and too black to read.
cache.forcelabel: Prise the planks off the end wall
cache.force: The nails scream coming out, and the noise goes away down every gallery. Prising the planks off is most of an hour's work. Behind them is a store-room.
cache.chamber: A store cut square into the rock and shelved with timber. Most of the shelves are bare; on the lowest, things have been laid out and covered with sacking.
cache.docshut: A tally-board hangs from a nail, notched and written on.
cache.doctext: The notches are the Delvers' count. The writing over them is {kingdom}'s: 'Taken into the king's keeping: the last of the paymaster's store. To be fetched when the shaft is cleared.' The shaft was never cleared.

order.chestseen: An iron strong-box is bolted to the floor. Three stamps are set into its lid: {a}, {b} and {c}. Each can be pressed down.
order.chestopen: The strong-box stands open, its lid thrown back.
order.friezeseen: A board on the wall is painted with the shifts, a sign for each. The first shift's sign is {first}. The second's is {second}. The night's is {third}.
order.known: The shift-board in the haulage gives the shifts in order: {first}, then {second}, then {third}.
order.held: The stamp goes down with a click and stays down.
order.wrong: The stamp goes down, and all three jump back up with a clang. The sound goes away down the galleries.
order.right: The last stamp goes down. Bolts slide inside the box, and the lid comes up.
order.readlabel: Read the paymaster's marks on the box
order.lore: Each stamp has a shift's number cut beside it in the Delvers' count: {first}, then {second}, then {third}.
order.loreno: The numbers by the stamps are rusted over. You cannot read them.
order.forcelabel: Prise the strong-box open by main force
order.force: It takes an hour of prising and the hammer of your boots. The lid tears open, and what was inside is broken.
